messages:
Maria (CS): FYI Sentinels Health (large regional provider) just asked to onboard a multilingual medical-translator model — wants support for EN/ES/PT and PHI-safe redaction by next release window. Contract renewal in ~3 weeks so this is time-sensitive.
Jared (Solutions): Do we have a precedent for PHI redaction + translation in a hosted flow? Private preferred?
Ivy (Security): We usually require Private (VPC + KMS/HSM) for PHI + audit logs. Need to confirm data residency for PT locale too. Also: will they pass test PHI flagged queries for our evals?
Ravi (Infra): From infra side we can stand up a Dedicated pool for canary. Latency target? 95th p90/p95 matters for their product. Quantized 13B will be cheaper but might degrade quality on medical terms.
Emily (Eng): For quality acceptance we'll run a 2-stage eval: (1) safety/regression on our PHI prompt set + synthetic bilingual test pairs, (2) domain accuracy against their curated clinical snippets. Metrics: BLEU-ish (translation), entity preservation, hallucination rate, and explicit PHI-redaction FPR/FNR. Need their gold dataset (we can redact tokens).
Maria (CS): They shared an initial CSV (10k rows) but with PHI. They've asked if we can do in-place evaluation or they prefer to share tokenized examples. They want a canary asap.
Jared (Solutions): Action items: 1) Ask legal to sign data exchange addendum for evaluation. 2) Request redacted sample + a sealed PHI dataset transfer plan. 3) Propose Private/Dedicated canary with rollback.
Ivy (Security): Agreed. Also require HSM key access policy and SIEM forwarding for the canary. I'll draft the checklist.
Ravi (Infra): For the canary config I'll need: model size (candidate: 7B-quant, 13B-int8), seq len expectations, batch size goal, and target p95 latency < 350ms for <256 token inputs. If they can't meet latency we should recommend streaming or caching first-token prefixes.
Emily (Eng): Quick sample eval command we'll run:
```
# eval harness snippet
python eval_runner.py --model candidate-13b-int8 --dataset sentinels_sample.jsonl --metrics translation,redaction,entity-f1
```
We'll also add a hallucination check with our hallucination prompts.
Maria (CS): Customer asked about cost impact. Can we give a back-of-envelope for Dedicated vs Private-hosted?
Jared (Solutions): Dedicated monthly commit estimate: ~2-3x hosted token cost but predictable throughput; Private (on-prem) we'd provide license + support quote. I'll draft numbers after Emily/Ravi pick model target.
Maria (CS): Scheduling: customer asked for an enablement + intake call tomorrow morning PST. I can host but need an engineer + security rep. Who can join?
Emily (Eng): I can join the intake for eval design 9:30am PST.
Ivy (Security): I can make 9:30 but may need 15 min late.
Ravi (Infra): I can join but can only stay for first 30 minutes (got deployment runway).
Jared (Solutions): I'll cover pricing and rollout plan.
redwood-deploy-bot: Meeting created: "Sentinels Health — Translator Onboard Intake" Thu 09:30 PST — invite sent to Maria, Jared, Emily, Ivy, Ravi.
Maria (CS): Great — final items before the call: please review the attached pre-intake checklist (PHI AAD, dataset transfer S3 presigned options, target SLOs). I'll paste the checklist in the call notes.
Emily (Eng): Prep note: ask them for 100 hand-labeled EN->ES/PT clinical pairs with entity annotations so we can compute entity-F1 quickly during the call.
Ivy (Security): I'll bring the minimal DPA checklist and our recommended KMS config.
Maria (CS): Also flagged: renewal risk high if we miss the window. I'll surface that on the call — if they delay evaluation more than 10 business days they may request a credit or look at competitors.
Jared (Solutions): Understood — aim to have canary proposal by EOD tomorrow after intake.
Maria (CS): Thanks everyone. I'll drop the meeting link and the customer's sanitized CSV in the thread post-call.
